figures.finding: Riga City Council's Riga Film Fund pays Latvian-foreign co-productions shooting in Riga and Latvia a cash rebate of up to 25% of eligible film-related expenditure once filming is completed, and can be combined with the co-financing the National Film Centre of Latvia administers (whose current terms could not be read; see blockers).

value.name: Riga Film Fund (Riga City Council)
value.eligible: Latvian-foreign co-productions shooting in Riga and Latvia
value.combinableWith: National Film Centre of Latvia co-financing

figures.applies: Riga and Latvia, as published by the city agency in 2026.

sources.said: Riga City Council co-financing programme “Riga Film Fund” is open to Latvian-foreign co-productions planning to shoot in Riga and Latvia. Up to 25% of eligible film-related expenditure can be obtained for the approved project as a cash rebate when filming is completed. … can be combined with the co-financing administered by the National Film Centre of Latvia.

figures.finding: Latvia's film industry counts 195 registered film producers and studios (city agency, 2026); in 2014 annual state support for film was EUR 4,041,639, only three Latvian features premiered in 2013 and six releases were expected in 2014, most of them co-productions.
figures.applies: Latvia; producer count 2026, funding and releases 2013-2014 (FNE, citing the period's figures).

sources.said: There are 195 registered film producers and studios represented in the industry.

The annual state support for film industry in 2014 is 4,041,639 EUR, which is over 1m EUR more than in 2013. … Although only three features premiered in 2013 … Six films will be released in 2014 … Most of the feature films released are coproductions

figures.finding: Latvia's National Film Centre funds new films by annual production competition: in 2022, 41 projects asked for EUR 6,672,951 and 16 were funded from EUR 1,982,472 (five features EUR 1,209,046, seven documentaries EUR 414,790, four animations EUR 358,636), a selection rate of about 39%.

sources.said: Nacionālajā Kino centrā noslēdzies 2022. gada jaunu filmu ražošanas konkurss ar pieejamo finansējumu EUR 1 982 472 ; atbalstīti 16 filmu projekti – piecas spēlfilmas, septiņas dokumentālās filmas un četras animācijas filmas. … konkursam tika iesniegts kopā 41 projekts, kopējais projektos pieprasītā finansējuma apjoms bija EUR 6 672 951. … No konkursā pieejamā finansējuma spēlfilmām tiks piešķirti EUR 1 209 046 (piecu pilnmetrāžas filmu ražošanas uzsākšanai), dokumentālajām filmām EUR 414 790 (septiņām dažāda garuma filmām) un animācijas filmām EUR 358 636

figures.finding: All public money a National Film Centre project takes, from any source, may not pass 50% of its eligible costs (80% for a 'difficult' film), under Cabinet Regulation No. 975 point 19 as worded from 30 April 2024.

value.rule: MK noteikumi Nr. 975 (12.10.2010), p. 19, as worded by MK noteikumi Nr. 265 (30.04.2024)

figures.applies: Latvia, projects the National Film Centre funds.

sources.said: 19.1. kopējais piešķirtā finansējuma apmērs neatkarīgi no finansējuma avota nepārsniedz 50 % no projekta kopējām attiecināmajām izmaksām. … 19.2. sarežģītas filmas veidošanai kopējais piešķirtā finansējuma apmērs neatkarīgi no finansējuma avota nepārsniedz 80 %

figures.finding: The Latvian co-financing programme for foreign productions pays 30% of eligible production costs for features and animation costing at least EUR 711,436 (documentaries EUR 142,287), with all public money held to 50% of the film's spend in Latvia (the National Film Centre's page, captured by Common Crawl on 2026-10-11).

value.name: Latvian co-financing programme for foreign productions

sources.said: An application can be made for international production service or co-production to receive a cash rebate of 30% on eligible production costs. The support can be combined with other public funding sources in Latvia in case if the Co-financing programme’s support together with other funding sources does not exceed 50% of the film’s total expenses in Latvia. … 711,436 EUR for feature and animation films … 142,287 EUR for documentaries
